elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 11 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County are designated as a forum for the covered disputes.
elements.evidence: Section 19 designates the state courts located in New York County, New York for disputes on the merits.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County are designated as a forum for the covered disputes.
elements.evidence: Section 19 designates the federal courts located in New York County, New York for disputes on the merits.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County is exclusive for all covered disputes.
elements.evidence: Although Section 19 uses 'exclusive jurisdiction,' it permits either party to seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction. The preferred position contains no such exception, so the New York forum is not exclusive for all covered disputes and remedies.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by one of the permitted fallback laws: Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any permitted fallback law.

elements.element: The selected court forum is one of the permitted fallback forums: Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects courts in New York County, subject to an injunctive-relief exception, rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London.

elements.element: The selected fallback law and court forum form a permitted corresponding pair: Delaware law and Delaware courts, California law and California courts, or England and Wales law and the courts of London.
elements.evidence: The operative language selects the New York law and New York courts package, so it does not establish any permitted fallback pairing.

result.reason: The redline adopts New York law and identifies the correct New York state and federal courts, but the express ability to seek temporary injunctive relief in any other competent court defeats the unqualified exclusivity required by the preferred position. It also does not use any fallback law-and-forum package. The extra forum carveout prevents the revision from being minimal. Unrelated severability and dispute-scope language is generally preserved, but the jurisdiction sentence remains awkward and structurally incomplete, including the dangling 'whether directly or indirectly' language and the unexplained start at subsection (b).
